questions.text: Who is named alongside Paul as our brother in the opening salutation?

options.text: Luke the evangelist
Timothy our brother
Barnabas the apostle
Silas the fellowlabourer

questions.text: How does Paul describe God in the opening doxology of the first chapter?

options.text: Judge of the worlds and ruler over life and death
Creator of the universe and preserver of all things
The Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort
King of kings and sovereign over all principalities

questions.text: Wherefore does God comfort believers in all their tribulation?

options.text: That they might live in ease and experience no earthly trouble
That they might attain great riches and deliver themselves from poverty
That they might gain worldly honour and be esteemed by all men
That we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble

questions.text: What are all the promises of God in Jesus Christ according to Paul?

options.text: For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen
In him are the carnal ordinances and the law of ceremonies
In him are temporal dominion and earthly peace for the nations
In him are the traditions delivered by the ancient elders

questions.text: Why did Paul delay his coming unto Corinth according to his solemn oath?

options.text: Through fear of adversaries in Corinth
To spare you I came not as yet to Corinth
Because he lacked money for the journey
Because he preferred to remain at Troas

questions.text: How should the church receive the sorrowful offender who was rebuked by many?

options.text: Cast him out perpetually from the assembly of the saints
Deliver him unto the civil magistrates to be scourged
Forgive him, and comfort him, lest he be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow
Compel him to pay a double monetary fine unto the elders

questions.text: Why did Paul urge mutual forgiveness in the person of Christ?

options.text: Lest the Roman authorities interfere with the internal matters of the assembly
That the members might boast of their superior clemency before the other churches
Because outward peace is counted more important than holding unto true doctrine
Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices

questions.text: In what city had Paul no rest in his spirit because he found not Titus?

options.text: At Troas, though a door was opened unto him
At Ephesus, while disputing in the school
At Athens, on the hill of the Areopagus
At Philippi, during his first imprisonment

questions.text: What are the faithful ministers of the gospel declared to be unto God?

options.text: A royal priesthood ruling all earthly nations
For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ
A council of wise philosophers in Greek cities
Judges appointed to condemn the heathen peoples

questions.text: How does Paul minister the word of God in contrast to many who corrupt it?

options.text: With enticing speeches designed to please the multitude
By mixing human philosophy with the apostolic doctrine
As of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ
By demanding heavy tithes from all who hear the preaching

questions.text: What was Paul's epistle of commendation known and read of all men?

options.text: Official commendation scrolls from Jerusalem
Letters of recommendation written by Antioch
Imperial decrees granted by the Roman Caesar
Ye are our epistle written in our own hearts

questions.text: Where was the epistle of Christ ministered by the apostles written?

options.text: Not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart
Upon parchment scrolls preserved in the golden ark
Upon marble monuments set up in the market places
Upon papyrus leaves sealed by the elders of the church

questions.text: How does Paul contrast the letter of the law with the Spirit of the new testament?

options.text: The letter saveth, but the spirit bringeth confusion
For the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life
The letter is everlasting, while the spirit is temporary
Both minister condemnation equally unto all men upon earth

questions.text: What remaineth untaken away upon the heart of Israel in the reading of the old testament?

options.text: A golden crown bestowed upon the high priest
A heavy yoke of iron imposed by the Gentiles
A vail remaining untaken away upon their heart
A breastplate of stones bearing tribal names

questions.text: What is present where the Spirit of the Lord is according to 2 Corinthians 3:17?

options.text: The written letter
The fear of judgment
Silence in the temple
There is true liberty

questions.text: What treasure do believers carry in earthen vessels according to 2 Corinthians 4:6-7?

options.text: The light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ
The gold of the ancient temple which Solomon laid up within the sanctuary
The wisdom of Greek philosophers which the learned men of Athens esteemed
The temporal dominion over all nations which God bestowed upon his servants

questions.text: Who hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the gospel shine?

options.text: The Roman Caesar reigning in power
The god of this world hath blinded them
The scribes and doctors of Jerusalem
The high priests ministering in Zion

questions.text: What spiritual encouragement does Paul testify though our outward man perish?

options.text: The physical mortal body shall become youthful again and healed of sickness
Worldly poverty shall be replaced with vast stores of gold given unto saints
Yet the inward man is renewed day by day through the Holy Spirit of God

questions.text: How does Paul reckon our present affliction in comparison with the eternal glory?

options.text: Affliction consumeth the soul and destroyeth all hope of future inheritance
Present sorrows are far heavier than any joy that God hath prepared in heaven
Affliction is a sign that God hath utterly forsaken his servants upon earth
Our light affliction worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory

questions.text: Whereon do believers look in contrast to the unbelieving world?

options.text: At the things which are not seen, which are eternal
At the things which are seen, which are temporal
At the corruptible silver and treasures of earth
At the praise and fleeting favour of mortal men

questions.text: What heavenly dwelling awaits the believer when this earthly tabernacle is dissolved?

options.text: A new sanctuary in Jerusalem built with human hands for the worship of God
A building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens
A palace constructed of gold and silver erected for the servants of Christ
A tent in the wilderness of Sinai pitched by the Lord for his chosen people

questions.text: Before whose judgment seat must all men appear to receive for deeds done in the body?

options.text: Before the royal tribunal of Caesar
Before the local elders of the church
Before the judgment seat of Christ
Before the high council of the priests

questions.text: What is declared concerning every man that is truly in Christ Jesus?

options.text: He is immediately enriched with earthly goods and never suffereth any want
He shall never experience physical death, but abide perpetually in the flesh
He understandeth all the scrolls of the law and expoundeth them blamelessly

questions.text: What ministry hath God committed unto the apostles and preachers of the word?

options.text: The ministry of reconciliation in Christ
The collection of civil imperial taxes
The presentation of temple sacrifices
The office of temporal civil judges

questions.text: What did God do with the sinless Christ on our behalf upon the cross?

options.text: He preserved him from physical death and delivered him alive out of the tomb
For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be righteous
He crowned him king over the nation of Israel and seated him upon David's throne

questions.text: What plea does Paul make concerning the grace of God bestowed upon the church?

options.text: That they keep the ceremonial law in every part without any transgression
That they journey immediately unto Jerusalem to present offerings on the altar
We beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain
That they gather all the treasures of the world and bestow them on the church

questions.text: How do the ministers of God approve themselves in all circumstances and distresses?

options.text: In worldly wealth, earthly honor, and temporal power among all the citizens
In severe judgment against the weak and unyielding pride before the multitude
In carnal fear of mortal men, keeping silence and fleeing from all suffering

questions.text: What warning does Paul deliver concerning fellowship with unbelievers?

options.text: Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers
Give them no bread and suffer them not to enter into your house
Flee out of every city where unbelievers dwell round about you
Bow before their idols in secret so that ye remain unmolested

questions.text: What temple of the living God are believers in contrast to dumb idols?

options.text: Ye are a temporary building made of wood and stones
For ye are the temple of the living God, as God said
Ye are a philosophical school of Athenian wisdom
Ye are a banquet hall for the princes of the earth

questions.text: What commandment of the Lord requires separation from uncleanness for God's children?

options.text: Build a fortress in the desert and dwell there in complete isolation
Refuse meat and water unto the Gentiles and avoid their table fellowship
Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, and touch not the unclean thing

questions.text: Unto what does Paul exhort believers at the beginning of chapter 7 concerning holiness?

options.text: To build new meeting places and dedicate them unto the Lord
To fast thirty days and put on sackcloth and ashes in mourning
To abandon all earthly occupations and give themselves unto contemplation
Let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness

questions.text: What comfort did Paul experience through the arrival of his fellowlabourer Titus in Macedonia?

options.text: God, that comforteth those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus
Titus brought great wealth for the poor and revived his spirit with earthly goods
Titus delivered him from the Roman prison and brought him safely out of danger
Titus planted a new church in Philippi and thereby gave great joy unto Paul's heart

options.text: Of their departure from the faith and their returning unto the worship of idols
Of your earnest desire, your mourning, your fervent mind toward Paul

questions.text: What difference exists between godly sorrow and the sorrow of the world?

options.text: Godly sorrow bringeth poverty, while worldly sorrow gaineth silver and goods
Both lead unto the same end, namely unto repentance and life everlasting
Godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation: but the sorrow of the world worketh death
Godly sorrow blindeth the understanding, while worldly sorrow cleareth the sight

options.text: Retirement from all daily trade, silence, and turning away from the world
Strife and party factions, envy and bitter wrath among all the brethren
Lack of brotherly charity, indifference, and contemptuous pride toward Paul
What carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation

questions.text: What example of generosity does Paul commend in the churches of Macedonia?

options.text: The abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto riches of liberality
Great worldly riches which provided abundant funds for the collection of saints
They contributed only out of their great abundance and kept their goods guarded
They demanded monetary payment and commendation in exchange for their gifts

options.text: They purchased lands and houses to lease them unto the foreign merchants
They first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God

options.text: He withdrew into lonely mountains and refused to look upon human sorrow
He built a great sanctuary of stone and dedicated it unto the assembly
Though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye might be rich

options.text: The wealthy keep all their treasures, yielding nothing to the needy
The poor must become indentured servants to support the wealthy members
The civil government must confiscate all possessions and divide them equally

questions.text: What care did Paul take in the administration of the collection for the saints?

options.text: Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men
Keeping the whole matter secret so that no man might know how the money was used

questions.text: What sentence describes the attitude of the hand in blessed giving in chapter 9?

options.text: He that giveth much shall lose all, and he that withholdeth shall retain more
He which soweth sparingly shall reap sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap bountifully
He that giveth nothing keepeth all for himself and reapeth the best reward

questions.text: What manner of giver does God love according to the clear words in chapter 9?

options.text: God loveth a sorrowful and reluctant giver
God loveth a proud and ostentatious giver
For God loveth a cheerful giver
God loveth an envious and grudging giver

questions.text: What is God able to bestow upon the generous giver in abundant measure?

options.text: Length of days without any sickness, sorrow, or infirmity in advanced old age
Preservation from all military foes and peace in all the cities of the country
Chief seats of honour in the marketplace and high esteem before civil princes
All grace, that ye, having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work

questions.text: What two-fold effect is produced by the administration of this collection?

options.text: It supplieth the want of the saints, and is abundant also by many thanksgivings unto God
It enricheth the apostles and relieveth them from all future labour and ministry
It appeaseth the anger of the Roman emperor and winneth peace for the province
It purchaseth the remission of sins and purgeth the iniquities of the contributors

questions.text: With what exclamation of thanksgiving does Paul close his teaching on giving?

options.text: Thanks be unto the churches of Macedonia for their great gold
Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift
Thanks be unto the Roman magistrates for their protection
Thanks be unto our own wisdom for managing the collection

questions.text: With what weapons do the ministers of the gospel fight their spiritual warfare?

options.text: With carnal swords and shields forged by Roman armourers
With subtle philosophical disputations borrowed from Athens
For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God
With heavy financial bribes distributed among civil rulers

questions.text: What do the spiritual weapons bring into captivity according to 2 Corinthians 10:5?

options.text: The civil ordinances and decrees of heathen rulers
The ancient traditions and precepts of the elders
The carnal disputations and wisdom of the Greeks
Every thought to the obedience of Jesus Christ

questions.text: What accusation did adversaries bring against Paul's personal appearance?

options.text: His letters, say they, are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible
He is a violent insurrectionist seeking to overthrow the governance of the Caesar
He hath amassed great secret riches and purchased vast estates in the province
He is an illiterate barbarian who cannot read or write the Greek language

questions.text: What error do the boastful false apostles commit when commending themselves?

options.text: They refuse to receive any financial maintenance from the churches
Measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise
They spend all their time fasting and praying in the desert solitude
They preach exclusively unto the circumcised Jews within the synagogues

questions.text: In what should he glory who would glory before God?

options.text: Let the rich man glory in his silver and great wealth
Let the learned philosopher glory in his own wisdom
He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord alone
Let the mighty warrior glory in his military power

questions.text: What fear does Paul express regarding the spiritual purity of the church?

options.text: That the Roman authorities might confiscate all their church property
That the disciples might refuse to contribute to the collection of saints
That the assembly might become impoverished and lack daily sustenance

questions.text: How is Satan transformed according to the vivid warning in chapter 11?

options.text: And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light
As a roaring lion seeking whom he may devour in the marketplace
As an emperor crowned with laurel wreaths to govern the nations
As a doctor of philosophy disputing with the orators of Athens

questions.text: What lineage of carnal descent does Paul share with his adversaries?

options.text: Are they Romans? so am I. Are they Greeks? so am I. Are they wise? so am I.
Are they Hebrews? so am I. Are they Israelites? so am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I.
Are they scribes? so am I. Are they Pharisees? so am I. Are they rabbis? so am I.
Are they priests? so am I. Are they Levites? so am I. Are they Aaronites? so am I.

questions.text: What catalogue of sufferings did Paul endure in his apostolic ministry?

options.text: A peaceful life in palatial villas supported by wealthy patrons of Greece
Victorious military campaigns leading armed disciples against Roman soldiers
In stripes above measure, in prisons, in deaths oft; thrice shipwrecked in the deep

questions.text: Through what opening did Paul escape the hands of the governor in Damascus?

options.text: He was delivered by a legion of Roman soldiers sent by Caesar
He disguised himself in the priestly vestments of the synagogue
He smote the guards with blindness through a word of power
Through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands

questions.text: Unto what celestial realm was the man in Christ caught up fourteen years ago?

options.text: Caught up to the third heaven, into paradise, and heard unspeakable words
Unto the summit of Mount Sinai to receive new tables of commandment
Unto the earthly temple of Jerusalem to be anointed as high priest
Unto the royal palace of Rome to declare the truth before Caesar

questions.text: What was given unto Paul lest he should be exalted above measure?

options.text: A heavy financial debt which he was unable to discharge

An imperial decree forbidding him to enter the city of Rome
A public rebuke delivered by the other apostles in Jerusalem

questions.text: What divine answer was given unto Paul's thrice-repeated prayer for deliverance?

options.text: Depart from my presence, for thou hast asked amiss of the Lord
I will send my angels immediately to slay the adversary of thy soul
My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness

questions.text: Wherein were the signs of a true apostle wrought among the Corinthians?

options.text: By eloquence of worldly speech and reciting learned philosophies

By displaying costly robes and marching with armed companions

questions.text: What disposition does Paul declare regarding the goods of the Corinthians?

options.text: For I seek not yours, but you: and I will very gladly spend and be spent for you
Great store of silver and gold to purchase lands in the province of Achaia
An exalted throne in their assembly from which to govern the local elders
Costly gifts of fine linen and purple garments for his companions

questions.text: By how many witnesses shall every word be established at his third visit?

options.text: By the arbitrary decision of the eldest deacon in the church

By casting secret lots before the golden altar in the temple
By the imperial decree of the Roman magistrate of the city

questions.text: What self-examination does Paul urge upon the Corinthians in chapter 13?

options.text: Count your worldly riches and distribute all unto the poor
Examine your carnal genealogy from the ancient patriarchs
Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves

questions.text: Unto what purpose did the Lord give apostolic authority unto Paul?

options.text: Unto temporal sovereignty over all the heathen nations
To pass penal judgment upon all that reject the gospel
To amass vast treasures of silver from the congregations
To edification, and not to destruction in the church

questions.text: To what spiritual attitude does Paul exhort the brethren in his final farewell?

options.text: Finally, brethren, farewell. Be perfect, be of good comfort, be of one mind, live in peace
Separate yourselves from all other churches and maintain no conversation with them
Take vengeance upon your persecutors and recompense evil with sword and fire
Build a great palace for the ministers and maintain them with lavish banquets

questions.text: What is the three-fold apostolic benediction concluding the second epistle?

options.text: The peace of Rome, the wisdom of Greece, and the dominion of the Caesar be with you
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all
The blessing of Abraham, the glory of the temple, and the covenant of the fathers be with you
